content:
oncall-bot: PAGING: SEV2 - serving-runtime: node(s) flapping due to GPU driver resets (Xid) in us-west-2. Pager: dylan is on-call.

oncall-bot: Alerts: increased 5xx for text-gen route /v1/generate (redwood-base-3b). Autoscaling triggered but pods are evicted by node flaps.

Dylan: I'm on it. Seeing node gpu-uw-12 with repeated nvidia driver resets in CloudWatch. Metrics: GPU ECC corrected errors spiking, then kernel Xid events.

Sara: +1. Logs from the runtime show OOM followed by kernel Xid 31 on that node, then kubelet marking NotReady. Suspect driver+firmware interaction.

Dylan: Posting quick logs: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=9876, 2026-03-15 18:45:12
[ 1234.567900] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 3456 (python) total-vm:12000000kB
```

Cheng: I see ECC corrected counts rising in the last 20m on uw-12 and uw-14. Might be a regressed driver version pushed during last maintenance. Checking cluster node image rollout history.

Devops-bot: Deployment note: nodepool gpu-us-west-2 was updated 2026-03-15 17:30 with driver v520.56 -> v525.12.

Dylan: For immediate mitigation I propose: 1) cordon uw-12 and uw-14; 2) drain pods with --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets; 3) add fallback capacity in region us-east-1 for serving-critical model group; 4) if driver reset persists after drain, reboot node or roll back driver.

Sara: Agreed. I'll open a temporary traffic rule to send new inference traffic to dedicated fallback pool (redwood-fallback) until nodes stabilized. Applying canary routing now.

Dylan: Running commands: ```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-uw-12 -n prod
kubectl drain gpu-uw-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n prod --force
```

Dylan: Drain in progress, pods evicting. Some long-lived KV-cache processes are blocking eviction; I'll force-delete after graceful period.

Cheng: I'm spinning up two extra nodes in gpu-fallback pool + increasing ReplicaSet for redwood-base-3b by 30%. Cloud autoscaler should pick up.

Devops-bot: autoscaler: scaleUp requested for gpu-fallback-pool -> +2 nodes. ETA ~4m.

Katie-cs: Heads up to impacted customers: Several pilot tenants in us-west-2 saw 5xx spikes for embeddings and slower retries. We're drafting a short status note. ETA 10m.

Sara: Traffic reroute applied. Early metrics show 60% of new requests hitting fallback pool, error rate dropping. Still seeing occasional 5xx from retries where pods were killed mid-request.

Dylan: After draining, I ran a quick smoltcp check and then `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` on uw-12, but dmesg still reports Xid 31 within 30s.

Dylan: Trying kernel driver rollback as next step. Will cordon uw-14 and repeat same sequence.

Cheng: I'm checking image/driver rollouts. We can roll back the driver to v520.56 which was stable for last 72h. Preparing a kube machine-image roll back.

SRE-Lead: Quick note: prioritize customer-facing routes. If node continues to throw Xid after driver rollback, plan for full node reboot and host firmware check. Could be GPU hardware degradation.

Dylan: Rollback plan executed on uw-12: switched driver to v520.56 and rebooted. Post-reboot dmesg: ```
[ 200.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=0, 2026-03-15 18:56:01
[ 200.123600] NVRM: GPU recovered from reset
```
Dylan: gpu-uw-12 came back NotReady -> Ready. Metrics show ECC corrected errors trending down but still higher than baseline.

Sara: Error rate back to baseline on /v1/generate for most tenants. A couple of customers still have delayed jobs due to evicted pods; we're replaying job queues.

Katie-cs: Sent preliminary status update to customers: "We've mitigated a GPU driver instability in us-west-2; traffic rerouted and nodes rolled back. Some jobs were retried. Working on full RCA and next steps."

Dylan: uw-14 is still showing intermittent Xid messages. I'm going to mark it for replacement (terminate + reprovision) if rollback doesn't hold through next 30m.

Cheng: Agree—schedule node replacement if more than two resets in 15m. Also opening a hardware ticket with cloud provider to run ECC health scan and GPU firmware validation.

Devops-bot: cloud-ticket created: CT-88421 (GPU ECC scan requested for uw-12 and uw-14).

SRE-Lead: Handoff: Dylan has been on this for ~45m. I'll take over monitoring and coordinate with infra during the next 30m. Dylan, summarize current state for handoff.

Dylan: Handoff summary: 
- Incident: GPU driver resets (Xid) causing node flaps in us-west-2.
- Mitigation completed: cordoned/ drained uw-12; driver rollback to v520.56; node rebooted and recovered. Traffic rerouted to fallback pool; autoscaler + extra replicas added.
- Remaining work: monitor uw-14 (possible replacement), cloud ECC health check, RCA for driver regression vs hardware.
- Customer impact: transient 5xx and latency spikes for generation/embeddings in us-west-2 for ~30-45m; bulk of traffic rerouted; customer notice sent.

SRE-Lead: Taking over. I'll keep this thread live. If uw-14 fails again, proceed with replacement and notify CS. Otherwise we'll close in 2 hours after stability window.

Katie-cs: I'll update the status page with current mitigation and ETA for RCA.

Dylan: Thanks all. Adding reaction :hammer: and signing off from active on-call.

sre-lead: Acknowledged. Monitoring dashboards set to 5m cadence. Next update in 15m or on change.
